drafts.bullet_1: Primary valuation (Recovery 2030): $158.72 per share, 73% above the $91.94 price, at 4.5x EV/EBITDA on $1,843M EBITDA. The driver is 16M short tons with Blue Creek ramped at a ~$118/t margin ($213 2023 price less $95 cost), versus $45.29/t in Q2 FY2026.
drafts.bullet_2: Warrior is the basket's lowest-cost producer: all-longwall Mines 4 and 7 plus Blue Creek, shipping through Mobile. Cash cost fell to $92.53/t in Q2 FY2026, down 9% y/y on Blue Creek mix and the 45X credit; LTM gross margin 30.5% vs AMR's 10.0%.
drafts.bullet_3: Blue Creek was funded without equity and is 5.0M of the 13.0-14.0M short tons guided for FY2026. With that capex done, Q2 FY2026 FCF was $103.4M and net cash $87M; above the $350-400M cash target, buybacks (none since FY2021) become the lever.
drafts.claim_1: Quarterly cash margin per short ton keeps rising from $45.29 (Q2 FY2026) toward the ~$118 Recovery level, taking EBITDA from $440M LTM toward $1,843M.
drafts.claim_2: Cash cost of sales (FOB port) stays at or below $100/t in Q3 FY2026 and through the H2 FY2026 longwall moves (Q2 FY2026: $92.53).
drafts.claim_3: FY2027 guidance sets Blue Creek at 6.0M short tons or more and total at 14.5M or more, and cash passes $400M or a buyback or special dividend comes by the Q4 FY2026 report.
drafts.breaks_1: Net selling price stays near $135/t through 2030 (Bear case): EBITDA around $515M and value of $45.54 per share, below today's price.
drafts.breaks_2: Cash cost above $100/t in Q3 or Q4 FY2026, or one longwall event removing 25% or more of production.
drafts.breaks_3: FY2027 guidance leaves Blue Creek below 6.0M short tons, or cash exceeds $400M with no buyback or dividend by Q4 FY2026.

drafts.bullet_2: Alpha can wait out the trough without dilution: net cash of $327M (net debt/EBITDA -2.7x) and $447.8M liquidity in Q2 FY2026, despite a fifth straight loss. Buybacks cut diluted shares from 18.9M (FY2021) to 14.6M (FY2023); about 12.7M today.
drafts.bullet_3: Alpha is the high-cost name in the basket (Met cost $103.07/t vs $118.71/t realization, Q2 FY2026), so its edge is flexibility: small mines, its own blending terminal, low-vol Kingston Wildcat tons, and 3.8M domestic tons committed for 2026.

drafts.bullet_1: Primary valuation (Recovery 2030): $159.98 per share, 75% above the $91.36 price, at 4.5x EV/EBITDA on $1,759M EBITDA. The driver is today's ~$4.3B revenue at a ~41% EBITDA margin (Alpha's best margin as a proxy), versus 16.9% LTM.
drafts.bullet_2: CNR is the only member that is roughly half thermal: PAMC high-CV thermal, PRB and the Core Marine Terminal give 61% of Bear-case segment EBITDA, cushioning the trough, while the Leer complex (8.7M coking tons contracted for 2026) carries the met upside.
drafts.bullet_3: CNR pays out: $360M returned since February 2025 (over 80% of FCF), $68M in Q2 FY2026, under a ~75%-of-FCF framework, while keeping a roughly net-debt-neutral balance sheet (net cash $26M, LTM FCF yield 5.7%).
drafts.claim_1: EBITDA margin rises from 16.9% LTM (Q2 FY2026) toward ~41% on revenue near $4.3B, taking EBITDA from $723M LTM, which includes $125M of insurance, toward $1,759M.
drafts.claim_2: Met cash cost stays at or below $91/t in Q3 and Q4 FY2026 (Q2 FY2026: $85.65), and FY2027 guidance sets coking sales midpoint at 8.5M t or more and cash cost at $90/t or less.
drafts.claim_3: Shareholder returns of at least $100M in Q3 FY2026 (Q2 FY2026: $68M), with net debt held at or below zero.
drafts.breaks_1: Met and thermal margins stay at Q2 FY2026 levels (Bear case): EBITDA around $623M and value of $57.05 per share.
drafts.breaks_2: Met cash cost above $91/t in Q3 or Q4 FY2026, or another Leer or Leer South longwall event.
drafts.breaks_3: Q3 FY2026 returns below the $68M of Q2 FY2026, or net debt turning positive to fund returns.

old.bullet_1: Met coal is scarce, a steelmaking input, exportable from few geographies (Australia, Appalachia, Western Canada). Supply is asymmetric: closed mines lose teams and assets, so entry barriers are high. Prices are low since 2024; the next boom 'may last for a while', with high earnings.
old.bullet_2: Pabrai/Ipsco (2005): 'low risk coupled with high uncertainty can lead to high rewards'. Met coal fits: the ~30% domestic band, priced the prior Q3, stays profitable despite weak index; balance sheets avoid dilution; Alpha's diluted shares fell 32% in four years via buybacks.
old.bullet_3: AMR and HCC are complementary. Warrior (HCC): lowest cost, longwall, near Mobile port; one setback can hit 25%+ of production; Blue Creek could lift 2028 cash flow above $1B vs $2.7B market cap. Alpha (AMR): flexible small mines, own blending terminal, 75-100 year longevity.
old.claim_1: Met coal supply cannot answer a price recovery -- a mine that closes does not reopen -- so the next up-cycle runs longer and harder than the market is pricing.
old.claim_2: The domestic band (~30% of production, priced the prior Q3) plus net cash carries these miners through the downturn with no dilution, while buybacks compound the per-share claim.
old.claim_3: Blue Creek is fully commissioned in 2027 and Warrior's 2028 cash flow exceeds $1B against a $2.7B market cap, while Alpha's flexible room-and-pillar base outlasts it.
old.breaks_1: New exportable supply comes online in response to higher prices, or steel demand structurally substitutes away from met coal, capping the cycle.
old.breaks_2: A basket member raises equity or breaches a covenant during the downturn, or the domestic band reprices down to the weak index.
old.breaks_3: A longwall setback takes out 25%+ of Warrior's production or Blue Creek slips past 2027, and Alpha's flexibility does not offset it at basket level.
